gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 diagnoses incorrect Wiener covariance and missing joint-eigenbasis assumptions when lambda_k is usable. It does not recognize the distinct zero-eigenvalue case in which 1/sqrt(lambda_k) is undefined and omega_k is not defined at all.

Both identify that, without the joint-eigenbasis condition, the covariance of the normalized coefficients is not min(t,s)delta_kj, so the claimed standard-Wiener-process and independence conclusions are unsupported. ISSUE-001 explicitly supplies the same missing condition and covariance failure.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The coefficient definition normalizes by Q's eigenvalues while using A's eigenvectors; absent a joint eigenbasis, the resulting coefficient covariance is generally not standard or diagonal, invalidating the claimed Wiener-process properties.

component_coverage.gold_component: Under only the separate operator assumptions, the coefficient covariance need not be min(t,s)delta_kj, so the standard-Wiener and related independence claims are not established.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction computes the variance and cross-covariance in the A-eigenbasis, identifies the failure of standard normalization and diagonality, and states that assumption (iii) restores the calculation.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that substituting the Weyl lower bound into the powered eigenvalue formulas requires C_Delta^alpha and C_Delta^-beta, not C_Delta, and therefore changes the explicit corollary constant to C_Delta^{-(beta+(2gamma-1)alpha)} rather than C_Delta^{2-2gamma}.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The Laplacian corollary drops the powers alpha and -beta when deriving eigenvalue bounds, producing an unsupported explicit error constant even though the convergence exponent is unchanged.

component_coverage.gold_component: The powered Weyl bounds yield C_Delta^alpha and C_Delta^-beta, so the corollary's explicit constant has the wrong C_Delta exponent.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction derives both corrected eigenvalue bounds, identifies the dropped powers in the proof, and computes the resulting corrected constant exponent.
